clue.text: Holiday firm supplies oysters

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, is a traditional British holiday weekend
firm means stable, steady

explanation.surface: A holiday company is in the business of providing oysters.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITSTABLE is a seaside town in Kent, England, long famous for its oyster beds; 'Holiday firm' reads as a travel company.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town is renowned for its native oysters and its annual oyster festival, so it is the place that provides them.

clue.text: Cape familiar to the matador?

explanation.surface: A bullfighter knows all about his cape.
explanation.walkthrough: The matador's cape is the red cloth he waves, but the first sense is a headland at the tip of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Horn is the headland at South America's southern tip, and a bull's sharp horn is what every bullfighter knows only too well.

clue.text: Disorder of one's stomach last month

parts.note: tum is the informal word for a stomach
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old commercial letters

explanation.surface: An upset stomach that someone suffered a few weeks ago.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old business-letter shorthand for 'of last month', as in 'your letter of the 5th ult.'
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is uproar and confusion, a state of disorder.

clue.text: He swears he's a soldier

explanation.surface: A man who curses a lot turns out to be in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'swear like a trooper' supplies the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier is called this, and the idiom 'swear like a trooper' makes the type of a habitual curser.

clue.text: A ship's prison

parts.note: names the lock-up aboard a naval vessel, and the word for it is also itself a kind of two-masted ship

explanation.surface: The cell where sailors are locked up aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: In navy usage the cells for detaining sailors aboard are called by this name, which also names a square-rigged two-master.

clue.text: You may be surprised if it goes up

definitions.text: You may be surprised if it goes up

parts.words: You may be surprised if it goes up
parts.note: reads like a market or a price rising unexpectedly, but describes the facial feature raised in astonishment

explanation.surface: Something whose rise would catch you off guard, like a price or a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the arch of hair above the eye is the classic facial sign of astonishment.

clue.text: In which the rider was carried on foot

definitions.text: In which the rider was carried on foot

parts.words: In which the rider was carried on foot
parts.note: a passenger seat borne on poles by two walking porters, so the traveller rode while others went on foot

explanation.surface: A conveyance where the passenger travelled while bearers walked.
explanation.definitionFit: This enclosed seat on poles was carried through streets by two porters walking front and back, common in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: One doesn't have to practise it

definitions.text: One doesn't have to practise it

parts.words: One doesn't have to practise it
parts.note: reads as something optional, but the practice in question is going without things, doing without

explanation.surface: A habit that is optional rather than required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have' is the trick: practising this virtue means one does not have, refusing oneself pleasures.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence and going without one's own wants is the virtue named; whoever practises it does without.

clue.text: He's on about being present

parts.note: he is taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man keeps going on about attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are in attendance, as at a roll call, is answered with this word.

clue.text: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it

definitions.text: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it

parts.words: The performer's bound to be uplifted by it
parts.note: reads as an artist certain to be inspired, but bound means a leap and uplifted means thrown into the air by springy canvas

explanation.surface: Something certain to inspire an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is a jump, not 'certain', and 'uplifted' is literal, not emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats bounce high on this sprung canvas frame, which throws them upward.

clue.text: Exist with just a part interest

parts.note: to be is to exist
a half is only a part of the whole

explanation.surface: Someone holding only a partial stake in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works through the phrase 'on behalf of', meaning 'in the interest of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's behalf means acting in their interest or for their benefit.

clue.text: Gossips with stories about island race

indicators.note: the stories sit about, around, the race letters

parts.note: tales are stories
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Gossips swapping yarns about a motorbike race on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorbike race on the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattle is to chatter idly or tell tales, so a person doing so gossips.

clue.text: A novice but he appears to have covered a lot of ground

definitions.text: A novice but he appears to have covered a lot of ground

parts.words: A novice but he appears to have covered a lot of ground
parts.note: a beginner who, taken literally, has sore soles as though from walking a long way

explanation.surface: A beginner who nonetheless seems to have travelled far.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word into its parts: someone with a sore sole looks like a long-distance walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer unused to hardship was called this, originally a settler not yet toughened to frontier life.

clue.text: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood

definitions.text: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood

parts.words: People responsible for the upkeep of the neighbourhood
parts.note: reads as caretakers of a district, but refers to the neighbours everyone strives to keep up with socially

explanation.surface: The folk who maintain the local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upkeep' alludes to the idiom 'keeping up with' the neighbours, matching their possessions and status.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of keeping up with the family next door describes the competitive striving for status among neighbours.

clue.text: Look around in the river

indicators.note: the look word goes around the in letters

parts.note: see is an instruction to look

explanation.surface: Someone peering about while standing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seine is the river flowing through Paris to the English Channel.

clue.text: A singular spectacle

parts.note: reads as a remarkable sight, but means one eyeglass rather than a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: An extraordinary sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' means one rather than remarkable, and 'spectacle' is the single lens of a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens worn in one eye is the singular counterpart of spectacles.

clue.text: Gold's a precious one that came across little Albert

parts.note: met means encountered, came across
Al is a short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: A gold item someone once encountered in young Albert's possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is classed as a precious metal, along with silver and platinum.

clue.text: Away to make newer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Away to make newer' (5): RENEW is an anagram of NEWER but no word is left to define the answer, so the clue looks misread in OCR and no source gives the printed text.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née, meaning born, introduces a maiden name

explanation.surface: Someone who entered and left the world penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of want or destitution is a synonym for being poor.

clue.text: Transport will be back at eleven

indicators.note: the word at is to come back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A ride will return at eleven o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car, a form of transport.

clue.text: He gives things away-but is not admired for it

definitions.text: He gives things away-but is not admired for it

parts.words: He gives things away-but is not admired for it
parts.note: reads like an unpopular philanthropist, but describes a telltale who gives secrets away

explanation.surface: A man who hands out gifts yet earns no thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives things away' means betrays secrets, not generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolyard telltale who informs on others is despised for disclosing their doings.

clue.text: Lax hands creep inside the ship

indicators.note: creep goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, used before a ship's name
to crawl is to creep

explanation.surface: Idle deckhands sneaking about inside a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' looks like sailors but means handwriting, and 'Lax' means careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless, untidy handwriting is called a scribble; a hand is a style of writing.

clue.text: VIP orders pink gin

indicators.note: orders as rearranges, putting the letters of the drink into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An important guest calls for a pink gin.
explanation.walkthrough: A pink gin is gin with Angostura bitters, a classic British naval drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important person in a group is called the linchpin figure, a big shot.

clue.text: Proclaim two points have little weight

parts.note: E, east, is one compass point
N, north, is the second compass point
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Declaring that a couple of matters carry slight importance.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or pronounce formally, to declare.

clue.text: Free of politics

explanation.surface: Something independent of political matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free of politics' looks like one phrase meaning apolitical; split it into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous or unrestricted is one sense, and the other names a member of the Liberal Party in British politics.

clue.text: Peers squeal when excited

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters of the word are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Lords shrieking in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like members of the House of Lords, but means those of the same standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers are people of the same rank, those one is on a level with.

clue.text: Feast I set out for a religious festival

indicators.note: set out as laid out afresh, the letters arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: Arranging a feast for a saint's day celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain and Latin America a saint's day is marked with a holiday celebration of this name.

clue.text: Smart boy

parts.note: a know-all lad, from the phrase smart followed by a boy's name

explanation.surface: A clever lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'smart Alec' means a cocky know-all, so the boy's name completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocky know-it-all is called a smart Alec, the name being a short form of Alexander.

clue.text: House in the Home Counties on the motorway

parts.note: SE, south-east, is the region of England containing the Home Counties around London
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A home in the commuter belt next to a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are those surrounding London, in England's south-east (SE); the M1 is a major British motorway, written MI with I for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A British semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour, is called by this short form.

clue.text: Oil rig sited in a good position

parts.note: an oil well is a drilling installation for oil
placed means sited, positioned

explanation.surface: An oil platform has been positioned in a favourable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being advantageously situated is to be ideally located or set.

clue.text: Warning that a man is about to cry

definitions.text: Warning that a man is about to cry

parts.words: Warning that a man is about to cry
parts.note: sounds like someone near tears, but is the call a town crier shouts before an announcement

explanation.surface: A sign that someone is close to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cry' means make a public proclamation, as a town crier does, not weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Town criers and court officers call out this word, meaning 'hear ye', to demand attention.

clue.text: The cricketer made another mistake

parts.note: a fielding position near the wicket in cricket, read literally as a further error

explanation.surface: A cricket player blundered again.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are fielders behind the batsman; this one stands next to first slip.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, and read as two words it means an additional error.
